heightHints: Single-nave church (trefoil plan) with one octagonal tower on a square base over the naos; low hipped roof over nave/apses. No measured height; from photos the eaves are roughly one storey above a tall plinth and the tower is about 2-2.5x eaves height (estimate only).
metalVisibleInPhotos: Commons photos are from 2014-2016, i.e. BEFORE the 2020 elZinc Slate purchase: they show a grey sheet-metal (probably galvanised) roof and tower cap. The new pre-weathered slate-grey zinc roof is not documented in the saved photos; geometry is what matters for the model.
verificationNotes: company says it has photos (not available to us). In Berca village the only skete is Schitul Sfinții Arhangheli Mihail și Gavriil ('Schitul Berca', former Berca monastery founded by stolnic Mihalcea Cândescu, 17th c.; LMI BZ-II-a-A-02363, church BZ-II-m-A-02363.01), OSM precinct way 1191315180 (amenity=monastery) and church way 217354519 (MRR 24.2 x 11.7 m, 207 m2). Alternative in the same commune: Mănăstirea Rătești (village Mânăstirea Rătești, OSM way 711952312, 5 km NW), but it is a 'mănăstire', not a 'schit', and was badly damaged by the 2014 landslide. Roof works of 2020 not confirmed by any public source; it is also possible the zinc went on an annex (cells) rather than the church. PROBABLE.

officialName: One Plaza Athénée – clădirea nefinalizată din Str. Georges Clemenceau 8-10 (proiectul Hotel Indigo București, 2018-2019)
altNames: Hotel Indigo Bucharest (IHG project announced 2018, never opened)
The Vendôme Palace & Galerie (2009-2010 hotel project on the same site)
One Plaza Athénée (One United Properties, 5-star hotel project from 2022)
address: Strada Georges Clemenceau 8-10, Sector 1, București (next to the Athénée Palace hotel and the Romanian Athenaeum)
heightHints: Reported as 5 above-ground floors + 3 basements (Profit.ro, Jan 2018: structure already erected, facade replicating a 19th-century building that stood on the site); 10,154 m2 gross, of which 6,410 m2 above ground, plot 1,361 m2 (Capital.ro/Profit.ro, Dec 2022).
metalVisibleInPhotos: No photos saved: only marketing renders of the One Plaza Athénée project were found (copyrighted, not the as-built state).
verificationNotes: No Hotel Indigo ever opened in Bucharest (IHG's first Romanian Indigo is Satu Mare). Chain of evidence: (1) Profit.ro 10 Jan 2018: IHG to open Romania's first Hotel Indigo (~100 rooms, 4*+) in central Bucharest near the Athenaeum, on the site prepared for 'The Vendôme Palace & Galerie' (halted by the 2008 crisis); structure already up, 5 floors + 3 basements, facade replicating a 19th-c. building. (2) 2009-2010 press (PressPort/The Diplomat): Vendôme Palace & Galerie = new-build luxury hotel next to the Athénée Palace Hilton at Str. Georges Clemenceau 8-10. (3) Dec 2022: One United Properties bought the 'unfinished, abandoned building' at Str. Georges Clemenceau 8-10 (3 basements, 10,154 m2) from Keys MS Clemenceau (Keys REIM) for EUR 13.5 m, to complete it as the 5-star 'One Plaza Athénée'. OSM way 1229725852 'One Plaza Athénée' (MRR 58.4 x 25.1 m, bearing ~180°) is the building next to the address node Str. Georges Clemenceau 8. So the 2019 zinc was very probably for the roof/mansard of this shell. Whether the roof was actually installed, and whether One United kept it, is not confirmed. PROBABLE.

address: Strada Panselelor 31, Sector 4, București (cartierul Apărătorii Patriei)
metalVisibleInPhotos: No photos saved: the only photo found is a copyrighted Basilica.ro (Mircea Florescu) image of the 2019 re-consecration; no free exterior photo located.
verificationNotes: Patriarch Daniel re-consecrated the church of the Apărătorii Patriei neighbourhood on 22 Sep 2019 (Basilica.ro / Orthodox Times / Pravmir, 22-23 Sep 2019) - a re-consecration normally follows major renovation, which matches the 2019 zinc purchase - and the reports say the church was founded by First World War veterans who settled there. Of the two Orthodox churches named after the district in OSM, 'Biserica Ortodoxă Apărătorii Patriei I', Str. Panselelor 31 (way 80540040, start_date 1935, MRR 24.5 x 13.2 m) fits the veterans' interwar foundation; the other, 'Sf. Ambrozie - Apărătorii Patriei', Str. Lunca Bârzești 3 (way 313039909) dates from 1948. The articles do not name the parish or mention the roof, so the link is inferred. PROBABLE.

officialName: Copertină în incinta sediului Episcopiei/Arhiepiscopiei Buzăului (structure not identified)

verificationNotes: a canopy (copertină) inside the precinct of the bishopric's seat, not a building. The material line is identical to the adjacent 'Manastirea Sitaru' line, and Sitaru monastery belongs to the Archdiocese of Bucharest, not to Buzău, so the location was very likely copied from the previous line; the seat of the (Arch)diocese of Buzău is the compound on Aleea Episcopiei, Buzău (OSM way 1189741935). Neither the canopy nor its true location can be confirmed. UNRESOLVED; A canopy is not a meaningful map/model object; consider dropping or attaching to the Buzău archdiocese site.
